arc.title: A Windy Saturday
b: On Saturday, Nia and her grandpa took her new red kite to the park.
The wind lifted the kite high above the pond.
Then the string caught on a branch, and the kite got stuck at the top of an oak tree.
Nia's eyes filled with tears.
m: Grandpa tugged on the string, but the kite did not move.
Nia jumped as high as she could.
Her friend Omar ran over with a long stick.
The stick was still too short to reach the kite.
e: Then Ms. Bell, the park worker, came by with her tall ladder.
She climbed up and unhooked the kite.
Nia gave her a big hug.
After that, they flew the kite in the open field, far from the trees.

paras.t: Rain tapped on the window all Saturday morning.
"Oh no, now we can't play soccer," groaned Jonah.
Lena pressed her nose to the glass. "I love rain! We can jump in puddles!"
"Rain spoils everything," Jonah said, and he flopped on the couch.
Dad came in with two raincoats. "Rain is good for my tomato plants," he said.
"Can we go outside?" asked Lena.
Dad said, "Yes, if you wear your boots."
"I'll stay inside where it's dry," said Jonah.
Lena splashed out the door. "This puddle is as big as a pond!" she shouted.
Jonah called from the window, "Rain is still no fun!"
Dad smiled. "My tomatoes are happy," he said.

Lena.text: Rain is great for jumping in puddles.

voices.title: A Name for the New Fish

paras.t: The class had a new orange fish, and it needed a name.
"Let's call him Bubbles because that name is cute," said Tia.
"Cute names are boring," Felix said.
Felix made a scary face. "Let's call him Shark!"
"He is too little to be a shark," Tia giggled.
Ms. Moon said, "A name should fit the fish."
"Shark fits because he swims so fast," Felix said.
Tia watched the fish blow tiny bubbles. "See? Bubbles fits better!"
Ms. Moon smiled and said, "Let's have the whole class vote."
Bubbles won by one vote.
"Okay, but he is still a shark to me," said Felix.

Ms. Moon.text: The class should vote on the name.

nobody.text: The fish needs a long name.

paras.t: Snow covered the park, and the big hill was white from top to bottom.
"Let's sled down the big hill!" shouted Ben.
"That hill is too steep," Kim said, holding her sled tight.
Ben pointed to the top. "It's the fastest hill in town!"
"Fast is not fun if you tip over," said Kim.
Grandma Pat said, "Start on the little hill and see how it goes."
"The little hill is too slow," Ben groaned.
Kim looked at the big hill again. "It still looks too steep for me."
Grandma Pat said, "Then you can both try the little hill first."
So they did, and Ben zoomed down laughing.
"Next time, the big hill!" Ben called.

Ben.text: The big hill is the best because it is fast.

Kim.text: The big hill is too steep.

nobody.text: The big hill is too icy.

paras.t: Domino, the new puppy, flopped down on his soft bed.
"Let's play tug-of-war with him!" said Owen.
"He looks tired," Nell whispered.
Owen grabbed the rope toy. "Puppies always want to play!"
Nell said, "Look, his eyes are closing. He needs a nap."
Mom came in with the leash. "He needs a walk first," she said.
"A walk is boring," Owen said.
"Shh, he's asleep now," said Nell.
Mom said, "Then the walk can wait until he wakes up."
"Okay, but then we play!" Owen said, and he dropped the rope toy.

Nell.text: The puppy is too tired to play.

voices.title: A Hot Day by the Sea

paras.t: The sun was hot, and the waves rolled in.
"The waves are the best part of the beach!" said Lia.
"Ow, the sand is burning my feet," Rami said.
Lia ran to the edge of the water. "Come jump the little waves with me!"
"The beach is too hot for me," said Rami.
Aunt Bea said, "Shells are the best part."
Aunt Bea held up a pink shell. "Look what the waves left!"
"Can we sit in the shade?" Rami asked.
"Not yet! One more wave!" Lia called.
Aunt Bea said, "Let's look for shells by the shady rocks."

Rami.text: The beach is no fun when it is this hot.

paras.t: Grandpa Joe put a bowl of broccoli on the table.
"Yum! They look like little trees," said Pablo.
"I don't like the taste," Ada grumbled.
Pablo picked up the biggest piece. "I'm a giant eating a forest!"
"Broccoli is yucky," said Ada, and she pushed her plate away.
Grandpa Joe said, "Broccoli helps you grow strong."
"I'm strong enough already," Ada said.
Grandpa Joe winked. "Try it with a little cheese on top."
"Cheese makes it even better!" Pablo cheered.
Ada took one tiny bite. "It's still yucky, but the cheese is good."

Grandpa Joe.text: Broccoli is good for your body.

"Look at this cool worm!" said Zoe.
"Ew, worms are slimy," Ike said, and he backed away.
Zoe held out her hand. "He tickles!"
Ms. Park said, "Worms help the garden. They make the soil soft."
"Can we keep him in a jar?" asked Zoe.
Ms. Park said, "No, he belongs in the soil, where he can help the plants."
"I still don't want to touch one," said Ike.
Ike peeked at the worm. "Okay, he can stay in the garden, far away from me."
"Bye, little worm," Zoe whispered as she set him down.

Ms. Park.text: Worms are good for the soil.

"I heard something buzz," Cal said, and he pulled up his blanket.
Dad said, "The tent has a net, so the bugs stay out."

"Tonight is the best night ever," said Uma.

"I'm trying to read my book," said Marta.
Grandpa Sol said, "A drummer practices soft beats, too."
"Soft beats are boring," Jay said.
Grandpa Sol tapped the drum gently. "Soft beats help you keep time."
"Soft beats are perfect for reading," Marta laughed.
Jay tapped softly. "Okay, this sounds like rain."

Grandpa Sol.text: Soft beats help a drummer keep time.

paras.t: Ezra and Pia were painting a birdhouse in art class.
"Let's paint it bright red," said Ezra.
"Birds might like green better," Pia said.
Ezra opened the red paint. "Red is the color of a fire truck!"
"Green would match the trees," said Pia.
Mr. Long said, "Birds do not care about color. You could paint the roof one color and the walls another."
"A red roof!" Ezra said.
"And green walls!" Pia said.
Pia dipped her brush in the green paint. "The walls will look like leaves."
Mr. Long smiled. "Now you both get your color."

lines.text: It was the first warm morning of spring.
Bear! The flowers are out! I can't wait to see them!
(yawning) Five more minutes. I'm so tired.
Everyone, line up! Rabbit first, then Bear. No pushing!
(rubbing his eyes) Why is everyone up so early? I want my nap.
I can't wait! I'm hopping all the way there!
Stop hopping, Rabbit. Walk in a line, like I said.
Bear stretched, and the three friends went to see the flowers.
(yawning again) The flowers are nice. I'll look at them after my nap.
Squirrel had hidden her best acorn, but now she could not find it.
Oh no, oh no! What if I never find it? What will I eat this winter?
(wiggling his tail) Maybe it grew legs and walked away! Ha ha!
That is not funny. I looked under every leaf!
(slowly) Take a deep breath. Where did you dig last?
(hopping in a circle) Maybe a worm is wearing it as a hat!
By the big rock, I think. But what if someone took it?
Let's look by the rock together, one step at a time.
The acorn was right next to the big rock.
See? It was playing hide-and-seek!

lines.text: Mira built a block tower taller than her head.
(standing tall) Look at my tower! I built it all by myself. It's the tallest one in the class!
(crossing his arms) Humph. Your tower used all the blocks. Now I have none.
(quietly) Um... I like your tower.
Thank you! I worked so hard on it. Did you see the top?
(stomping his foot) I never get the blocks. This is not fair!
(looking down) You can have my blocks, Otto.
Otto took the blocks and stopped frowning.
Well... thanks. I guess.
Dark clouds rolled over the pond.
Rain is coming! Hooray! I love splashing in the rain!
(shaking) Did you hear that thunder? What if the storm lasts all night?
(slowly) Storms always pass. We can wait under the big leaf.

The leaf is strong. Sit close to me.

(peeking out) Oh! The storm is over.

Kit, you pour the lemonade. Sam, you hold the sign. I will count the cups. Go!

(smiling big) My volcano is the best one here. It took me a whole week to make!

(gently) Your plant looks healthy, Cleo. Just tell what you saw.
Watch this! The lava comes out right here. I made it all myself!
But what if I forget everything?
Then look at your poster. It has all your notes.

(taking a deep breath) Okay. I can do this.
Rain fell all day, so Cat and Dog stayed inside.
(wagging his tail) Let's play fetch in the hall! Or tag! Or both!
(flicking her tail) No. Rain is wet. Wet is bad. Leave me alone.
Squawk! Rain, rain, go away, come again on Tuesday! Squawk!
Come on, Cat! Just one game!
Humph. I'm not moving from this pillow.
Squawk! A cat on a pillow is a pillow-cat! Ha!
Dog played fetch by himself, and Parrot sang to the rain.
(grumbling) Too much noise for a rainy day.

You can sit here. No, there. Put your bag on the hook. Hurry, the bell is ringing!
(softly) Okay... um, thank you.

versions.text: Three little pigs lived in the woods. One day, they each built a house. The first pig built a house of straw. The second pig built a house of sticks. The third pig built a house of bricks. Then a big wolf came by. He wanted to catch the pigs. He huffed and puffed and blew the straw house down. He huffed and puffed and blew the stick house down. The pigs ran into the brick house. The wolf huffed and puffed, but the brick house did not fall. At last, the tired wolf ran away into the woods, and the pigs were safe.
